source.name: BBC Urdu: ’ماننا پڑے گا کہ پاکستان نے بہترین انتخاب کیا‘: انڈیا میں مصدق ملک کی ’غالب ڈپلومیسی‘ کا چرچا
source.author: Shakeel Akhtar

intro: Published 20 November 2026. At a Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) forum in Delhi, Pakistani minister Musadik Malik switched from English to Urdu and spoke about Mirza Ghalib, the great 19th-century poet of Delhi, and the speech was praised on social media in both countries. Ghalib is buried in Delhi's Nizamuddin neighbourhood; notice the respectful “daada huzoor” and “tashreef laana” in his speech.

sentences.urdu: ’سیاست کبھی بھی ادب، شاعری، موسیقی، ثقافت، کھانوں، فیشن اور زبان پر ہمارے مشترکہ فخر کو ہم سے چھین نہیں سکتی۔
sentences.english: ‘Politics can never snatch from us our shared pride in literature, poetry, music, culture, food, fashion and language.

sentences.urdu: کہنا پڑے گا کہ پاکستان نے اپنی نمائندگی کے لیے بہترین انتخاب کیا ہے۔‘
sentences.english: It has to be said that Pakistan has made the best choice for its representation.’

sentences.urdu: یہ کہنا ہے کہ انڈین صحافی اور مصنف غزالہ وہاب کا جو تین برسوں میں انڈیا کا دورہ پہلے پاکستانی وزیر مصدق ملک کی ایک ویڈیو پر تبصرہ کر رہی تھیں۔
sentences.english: So says the Indian journalist and author Ghazala Wahab, who was commenting on a video of Musadik Malik, the first Pakistani minister to visit India in three years.

sentences.urdu: پاکستان کے وفاقی وزیر برائے موسمیاتی تبدیلی مصدق ملک شنگھائی تعاون تنظیم (ایس سی او) کے پہلے تہذیبی مکالمے (سولائزیشن ڈائیلاگ فورم) میں شرکت کے لیے دلی میں موجود ہیں۔
sentences.english: Pakistan's Federal Minister for Climate Change, Musadik Malik, is in Delhi to take part in the first civilisational dialogue (the Civilisation Dialogue Forum) of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO).

sentences.urdu: سنیچر کے روز کانفرنس کے دوران ان کے خطاب کی ایک ویڈیو سوشل میڈیا پر موضوعِ بحث بنی رہی۔
sentences.english: On Saturday a video of his speech during the conference remained a topic of discussion on social media.

sentences.urdu: ایس سی او سولائزیشن ڈائیلاگ فورم سے خطاب کرتے ہوئے مصدق ملک نے کہا ’بڑا عجیب سا لگا کہ چند کوس دور غالب کے مقبرے سے یہاں بیٹھ کر میں انگریزی میں بات کر رہا ہوں۔‘
sentences.english: Addressing the SCO Civilisation Dialogue Forum, Musadik Malik said: ‘It felt rather strange that, sitting here a few kos from Ghalib's tomb, I am speaking in English.’

sentences.urdu: ’جی میں یہی سمایا کہ آج آپ سے اپنے دل کی آواز اردو میں بات کروں۔‘
sentences.english: ‘So it came into my heart that today I should speak to you in Urdu, in the voice of my own heart.’

sentences.urdu: مصدق ملک نے اپنی بات جاری رکھتے ہوئے کہا کہ ’اور کیسی عجیب سی بات ہے کہ غالب، جن کے دادا حضور سمر قند سے تشریف لائے تھے، یہاں نظام الدین آپ کے پہلو میں ان کی تدفین ہے، اور غالب جو اپنے آپ کو فارسی کا بہت بڑا شاعر جانتے تھے، ان کو پوری دنیا اردو کی وجہ سے پہچانتی ہے آج۔‘
sentences.english: Continuing, Musadik Malik said: ‘And how strange it is that Ghalib, whose revered grandfather came from Samarkand, is buried here at Nizamuddin, right beside you, and that Ghalib, who considered himself a very great poet of Persian, is known to the whole world today because of Urdu.’

چھین: snatch (“chheen nahin sakti” = cannot snatch away)
کہنا: to say (“kehna paṛe ga” = it has to be said; “yeh kehna hai … ka” = this is what … says)
پڑے: (“kehna paṛe ga” = one will have to say)
لیے: for (“ke liye” = for; in order to)
غزالہ: Ghazala (Ghazala Wahab, Indian journalist and author)
دورہ: visit (“X ka daura karna” = to visit X)
پہلے: first (oblique) (“pehle paakistaani wazeer” = the first Pakistani minister)
مصدق: Musadik (Musadik Malik, Pakistan's federal minister for climate change)
رہی: (continuous / “remained”, f.) (“kar rahi theen” = was doing; “bani rahi” = remained)
شنگھائی: Shanghai (“shanghaai taawun tanzeem” = Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, SCO)
شرکت: participation (“shirkat ke liye” = to take part)
دلی: Delhi (the Urdu name of the city)
موجود: present (“maujood hain” = is there, is present)
خطاب: address; speech (“X se khitaab karna” = to address X)
موضوعِ: topic of (“mauzoo-e behas” = topic of discussion)
ہوئے: (“karte hue” = while doing; “jaari rakhte hue” = continuing)
بڑا: big; great; very (“baṛa ajeeb sa” = rather strange; “bohat baṛa shaair” = a very great poet)
کوس: kos (an old measure of distance, about 3 km)
دور: far (“chand kos door” = a few kos away)
غالب: Ghalib (Mirza Ghalib, 19th-century Urdu and Persian poet of Delhi)
بات: talk; matter (“baat karna” = to talk; “ajeeb si baat” = a strange thing)
جی: heart; mind (“jee mein samaana” = to come into one's heart)
سمایا: filled; entered (“jee mein yahi samaaya” = this is what came into my heart)
کروں: (that) I do (subjunctive) (“baat karoon” = that I should speak)
کیسی: how; what a (f.) (“kaisi ajeeb si baat” = how strange a thing)
جن: whom; whose (pl. / respectful, oblique) (“jin ke daada” = whose grandfather)
حضور: honoured sir (respectful title; “daada huzoor” = revered grandfather)
سمر: Samar (“samar qand” = Samarkand, city in Central Asia)
لائے: brought (“tashreef laaye the” = had come, honorific)
نظام: Nizam (“nizaam ud-deen” = Nizamuddin, the Delhi neighbourhood around the Sufi shrine of Nizamuddin Auliya)
پہلو: side (“aap ke pahloo mein” = right beside you)
تدفین: burial (formal) (“un ki tadfeen hai” = he is buried)
جانتے: knew; considered (“apne aap ko … jaante the” = considered himself)
ان: his; him (respectful, oblique) (“un ke khitaab” = his speech; “un ko” = him)

options.english: That he was speaking English while sitting near Ghalib's tomb

options.english: That it was very cold in Delhi
